title: Implement quantity merge rules for aggregated items
description: Add the quantity accumulation logic inside the aggregator so exact-unit numeric quantities sum while mismatched units, text quantities, and quantity-less occurrences remain represented according to spec.
acceptance_criteria: Numeric quantities sum only when both values are `.number` and their units match after lowercasing and trimming, with `nil` matching `nil`.
The retained merged unit uses the canonical lowercased form derived from the first matching numeric occurrence.
Text quantities never merge and remain as separate entries in encounter order.
Quantity-less occurrences do not add `Quantity` entries but still ensure the aggregated item exists, including the all-quantity-less case with an empty `quantities` array.
Mixed quantity-less and quantified occurrences produce one aggregated item whose quantity list reflects only the quantified entries.
No unit conversion, plural normalisation beyond aisle aliases, or recipe-note preservation is introduced.

handoff_summary.completed: Applied two targeted changes to `ShoppingList.mergeQuantity(_:into:)`: (1) changed `.whitespaces` → `.whitespacesAndNewlines` in both unit comparisons to match the spec's trimming specification; (2) in the `else` branch (first numeric occurrence of a unit key), replaced `quantities.append(quantity)` with `quantities.append(Quantity(value: .number(newValue), unit: newUnit))` so the stored unit is the canonical lowercased+trimmed form rather than the raw input string. All other merging logic (nil-unit matching, text-quantity passthrough, quantity-less ingredient handling) was already correct and left unchanged.
handoff_summary.remaining: No remaining implementation work. Tester agent should verify all six acceptance criteria, particularly the unit-case normalisation scenario: `[100 G flour] + [50 g flour] → quantities: [Quantity(value: .number(150), unit: "g")]`.
handoff_summary.risks: None identified. Change is confined to a single private function with no API surface impact.
handoff_summary.next_action: Hand off to tester agent to verify all acceptance criteria against unit tests.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: No conflict risks. Only `Aggregation.swift` was modified in its private `mergeQuantity` function. No public API surface changed.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Chose to normalise the unit at append time (storing `newUnit` instead of `quantity.unit`) rather than at read time, keeping the stored data canonical and avoiding repeated normalisation on every comparison. The `quantities[idx].unit` on the sum path remains correct because it now always holds an already-normalised value from the first-occurrence append.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: No tests written in this bead (tester bead owns that). Key scenario to cover: mixed-case unit on first occurrence (`G`) merging with second occurrence (`g`) should produce unit `g` in the result.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: None. All six acceptance criteria are satisfied by the implementation as confirmed by code review and successful build.

conflict_risks: No conflict risks. Only `Aggregation.swift` was modified in its private `mergeQuantity` function. No public API surface changed.

execution_history.summary: Fixed `mergeQuantity` in `Aggregation.swift` to store the canonical lowercased+trimmed unit when appending the first numeric occurrence of a quantity, and updated the trim character set to `.whitespacesAndNewlines` per spec. Build passes cleanly.
